note: This file contains ONLY records whose every populated field was read from an official government source and recorded in datasets/raw/government/<id>/collection.json. It is deliberately small. See docs/datasets/government-schemes.md for why, and for the collection procedure needed to extend it. No record here was generated, inferred or completed from memory.

records.department: Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade
records.targetBusinessTypesNote: Derived from the stated requirement that Indian promoter shareholding be at least 51% as per Companies Act 2013 and SEBI (ICDR) Regulations 2018, which presupposes a company. The source does not enumerate permitted legal forms, so this is marked as DERIVED, not quoted.
records.supportedIndustriesNote: The official page states the scheme is 'Sector-agnostic', so no industry restriction is recorded. A separate preference list exists and is stored in preferenceSectors; a preference is not an eligibility restriction and is deliberately not used as a matching filter.
records.supportedStagesNote: Derived from the stated requirement that the startup be incorporated not more than 2 years ago and be seeking proof-of-concept and prototype funding. The source does not use stage labels, so this mapping is marked DERIVED.
records.supportedLocationsNote: Official page describes a 'PAN-India startup programme'. No state restriction stated.
records.supportedFundingTypesNote: Quoted: 'A startup applicant can avail seed support in the form of grant and debt/convertible debentures each once'. Convertible debentures are mapped to EQUITY because they convert; debt is mapped to CREDIT_SUPPORT.
records.fundingAmountDescription: Per-startup funding ceilings are not stated on the official pages collected. The scheme has a total outlay of INR 945 crore and is stated to support an estimated 3,600 entrepreneurs through 300 incubators over four years. Per-startup limits are expected in the official guidelines PDF, which has been identified but not yet collected.
records.totalOutlayNote: Quoted as 'an outlay of INR 945 Crore'. This is the scheme's total budget, NOT a per-applicant amount, and must never be presented as one.
eligibilityCriteria: A startup, recognized by DPIIT, incorporated not more than 2 years ago at the time of application.
The startup must have a business idea to develop a product or a service with a market fit, viable commercialization, and scope of scaling.
The startup should be using technology in its core product or service, or business model, or distribution model, or methodology to solve the problem being targeted.
Shareholding by Indian promoters in the startup should be at least 51% at the time of application to the incubator for the scheme, as per Companies Act, 2013 and SEBI (ICDR) Regulations, 2018.
A startup applicant can avail seed support in the form of grant and debt/convertible debentures each once as per the guidelines of the scheme.
ineligibilityCriteria: Startup should not have received more than Rs 10 lakh of monetary support under any other Central or State Government scheme. This does not include prize money from competitions and grand challenges, subsidized working space, founder monthly allowance, access to labs, or access to prototyping facility.
records.eligibilityRulesNote: Only the two machine-checkable gates that are unambiguously stated. The technology-usage, market-fit, promoter-shareholding and prior-support conditions are real criteria but are not reliably machine-checkable from the profile fields collected, so they remain human-readable criteria only. The engine reports them for verification rather than silently passing them.
records.businessAgeRequirement: Incorporated not more than 2 years ago at the time of application.
records.registrationRequirement: DPIIT recognition is required. The official page links to https://www.startupindia.gov.in/content/sih/en/startupgov/startup_recognition_page.html
records.documentRequirementsNote: Not enumerated on the pages collected. Expected in the guidelines PDF.
records.applicationProcess: The Seed Fund is disbursed to eligible startups through eligible incubators across India. Applications are accepted year-round, and startups can apply to 3 incubators simultaneously. Physical incubation is not mandatory. An Experts Advisory Committee constituted by DPIIT evaluates and selects incubators for allotment of Seed Funds.
records.applicationPortal: Startup India Seed Fund Scheme portal
records.applicationWindowNote: As displayed on the official site at the collection date: 'Final Notice (Extended): Last date for startups to apply under SISFS - 31 May 2026 | Incubators to complete 100% startup selection by - 30 June 2026.' This is time-sensitive and must be re-verified before being shown to a user.
records.sourceDateNote: Date the scheme was notified, quoted as 'notified on 21.01.2021'. Not the page's own publication date, which is not stated.
records.verificationNote: Every populated field above was read from a rendered official page on the collection date and is recorded verbatim in the raw collection file. Fields absent from those pages are null with a stated reason. This record is complete enough to publish, with the per-startup funding ceiling explicitly reported as unavailable.
records.schemeStatusNote: The official site displayed a current application deadline of 31 May 2026 at the collection date, which establishes the scheme as active rather than inferring it from the page existing.
records.notes: Per-startup funding ceilings are the one materially important field still missing. They are expected in the official guidelines PDF linked from the site. They have deliberately NOT been filled in from general knowledge.

records.provider: MUDRA (Micro Units Development & Refinance Agency Ltd)
records.targetBusinessTypesNote: The collected page does not enumerate permitted legal forms. It refers to 'micro units' and 'individual entrepreneurs' without restricting legal structure, so no restriction is recorded.
records.supportedIndustriesNote: The page describes non-farm income generating activities across trading, services and manufacturing without restricting to named sectors, so no industry restriction is recorded.
records.supportedStagesNote: The page states no business-age or stage requirement. Recording a stage list would invent a restriction the source does not impose.
records.supportedLocationsNote: A central scheme delivered through banks, NBFCs and MFIs; no state restriction is stated on the page.
records.supportedFundingTypesNote: Quoted: 'MUDRA provides refinance support to Banks / MFIs / NBFCs for lending to micro units having loan requirement upto 20 lakh.'
supportedPurposes: Term loan for micro enterprise activity
Shops, trading, service enterprises and non-farm income generating activities
records.fundingAmountDescription: Four categories are quoted on the page: 'Shishu : covering loans upto 50,000/-', 'Kishor : covering loans above 50,000/- and upto 5 lakh', 'Tarun : covering loans above 5 lakh and upto 10 lakh', 'Tarun Plus: covering loans above 10 lakh and upto 20 lakh'. The page further states 'MUDRA loans, i.e., loans up to 20 lakh, have been made collateral free, as per the RBI norms in this regard.' No minimum is stated, so minFunding is null.
records.totalOutlayNote: Not stated on the collected page.
eligibilityCriteria: Micro units having a loan requirement upto 20 lakh.
Non-farm income generating activities in trading, services and manufacturing.

Purchase of transport vehicles for transportation of goods and passengers such as auto rickshaws, small goods transport vehicles, 3 wheelers, e-rickshaws, taxis. Tractors, tractor trolleys and power tillers used only for commercial purposes are also eligible.
Setting up micro enterprises by purchasing necessary machinery or equipment with per beneficiary loan size of upto 20 lakh.
records.eligibilityRulesNote: No machine-checkable rules recorded. The page states activity categories rather than numeric thresholds a profile could be tested against, apart from the loan ceiling already captured in maxFunding.
records.documentRequirementsNote: Not enumerated on the collected page; documents are set by the lending institution.
records.applicationProcess: Loans are delivered through member lending institutions. The page states MUDRA provides refinance support to Banks, MFIs and NBFCs, which in turn lend to micro units; applicants approach a lending institution rather than MUDRA directly.
records.applicationWindowNote: No application window stated; the page describes an ongoing refinance facility.
records.sourceDateNote: The page carries no publication or last-updated date.
records.verificationNote: Collected directly from the official MUDRA site on 2026-10-11 and quoted verbatim. Loan band figures and the collateral-free ceiling are taken word for word from the page. Ministry and department are left null because the collected page does not state them; they were not filled in from outside knowledge. Not cross-checked against the PMMY governing circular.
records.schemeStatusNote: The page presents the scheme as currently operating. No closure date is stated.
records.notes: Tarun Plus (above 10 lakh and upto 20 lakh) raises the ceiling above the widely cited 10 lakh figure. The 20 lakh ceiling here is what the official page states as at the collection date.
